svg.title: The King Comes Twice
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 6 panels. Two columns side by side: He came on a donkey and He comes on a white horse, row for row. Panel 1 (Luke 19:35-38): Jesus rides a donkey's colt with cloaks on its back down a hillside; disciples walk ahead raising their hands. Caption: "Jesus comes down the Mount of Olives on a colt." The crowd of disciples says: "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven". Panel 2 (Revelation 19:11-12): Jesus rides a white horse out of opened heaven, many crowns on His head, with gold light behind. Caption: "Heaven opened, and a white horse." John says: "in righteousness he judges and makes war." Panel 3 (Luke 19:41-42): Jesus on the colt stops and weeps, looking toward the city out of the picture. Caption: "He drew near and saw the city." Jesus says: "Would that you, even you, had known on this day the things that make for peace!" Panel 4 (Revelation 19:14-15): Jesus on the white horse leads; behind Him riders in white linen on white horses. Caption: "The armies of heaven follow Him." John says: "From his mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations". Panel 5 (Matthew 21:5, 10-11): Jesus on the colt in a city street; a man in the crowd answers. Caption: "Jerusalem is stirred: “Who is this?”" Matthew says: "Behold, your king is coming to you, humble". A man in the crowd says: "This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee." Panel 6 (Revelation 19:16): Jesus on the white horse, nearer, crowns on His head. Caption: "The name on His robe." John says: "On his robe and on his thigh he has a name written, King of kings and Lord of lords." A strip joins the panels above: βασιλεύς, “king”: the same word at both comings. The point: One King comes twice. He came on a donkey to save the world (John 12:47) and make peace by His cross (Colossians 1:20), and He will come on a white horse to judge and reign (Revelation 19:11). Come to Him now, while He comes to you in peace.
svg.text: A donkey and a white horse, in one minute
HE COMES ON A WHITE HORSE
βασιλεύς, “king”: the same word at both comings
One King comes twice. He came on a donkey to save the world
(John 12:47) and make peace by His cross (Colossians 1:20), and
He will come on a white horse to judge and reign (Revelation
19:11). Come to Him now, while He comes to you in peace.
Jesus is drawn on the colt, which Mark, Luke and John say He sat on.
The diadems are Revelation 19:12's; the eyes like fire, the robe
dipped in blood and the sword from His mouth are left to the text.
